claims.text: flutter build web generates the app, including its assets, into the build/web directory of the project; the compiled Dart code of a release web build is main.dart.js.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: deployment/web.md (Building the app for release: 'places the files into the /build/web directory'); outputs/stage-3/scripts/frontend/web-bundle.txt

claims.text: build/web/canvaskit/ holds several builds of Flutter's engine; a browser downloads only the one it needs, and never the .symbols files, which are for debugging.
flutter build web compiles the Flutter framework code and the code of the app's packages that the app calls into the same main.dart.js as the app's own code.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: resources/faq.md (tree shaking: 'If you import a huge Dart library but only use a ... two-line method, then you only pay the cost of the two-line method'); deployment/web.md

claims.text: In a release build tree shaking has been performed: code the app never uses is left out, so importing a large package costs only the parts the app calls.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: testing/build-modes.md#release ('The build is minified and tree shaking has been performed'); resources/faq.md (tree shaking)

claims.text: Release web builds tree-shake icons: the build generates an icon font holding only the icons the app uses.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: release-notes-3.10.0.md ('tree shake icons from web builds'); blog accessible-expression-with-material-icons-and-flutter (custom icon font)

claims.text: Text such as main.dart.js shrinks a lot under gzip; web-bundle.sh shows its raw size and its size after gzip -9.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: scripts/frontend/web-bundle.sh:13-24; run the script after scripts/up.sh

claims.text: Compression: the client lists accepted codings in Accept-Encoding, the server names the coding applied in Content-Encoding, and the client decodes the content to get the original representation.

The Caddy encode directive with no format arguments enables zstd and gzip, compresses a response only when the client's Accept-Encoding allows a supported format, and leaves files on disk unchanged; a client sending no Accept-Encoding gets the uncompressed response.
claims.source_hint: Caddy docs: caddyfile/directives/encode ('If no formats are specified, gzip and zstd are enabled by default'); deploy/app-web/Caddyfile:16-21 @ stage-3

claims.text: At stage-3 deploy/app-web/Caddyfile adds encode before file_server, and a GET of :8081/main.dart.js with Accept-Encoding: gzip is answered with Content-Encoding: gzip.

In the stage-3 output, most of the eight largest files under build/web are engine builds under canvaskit/ (.wasm), with main.dart.js among them; 'all files together' counts every engine build and the .symbols file.
At stage-3 scripts/up.sh builds DonHang.App/build/web with flutter build web and starts app-web, which serves it on :8081.
The app's dependencies are listed in pubspec.yaml; check the bundle size (e.g. with web-bundle.sh) whenever you add one, because each can add code to main.dart.js.
claims.source_hint: outline item 5; refs/flutter-website: resources/faq.md (tree shaking: you pay for what you use)

claims.text: Every file the app needs must arrive before the first frame on any connection; a faster link shortens the wait but does not remove it, and a first visit has no cached copy.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: platform-integration/web/initialization.md (bootstrap loads main.dart.js and engine before running the app); foundation.l1.http-caching
